approved: Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013
John Hogg Order! The time allotted for the consideration of these bills has expired. The question is that the amendment on sheet 7404 moved by Senator Mason be agreed to.

The No votes succeeded in rejecting amendments proposed by Greens [Senator Wright](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Penny_Wright&mpc=Senate&house=senatein). This vote means that the amendments will not be included in the legislation. Someone who votes aye for this amendment supports these measures. The majority voted no for this amendment so it was unsuccessful. **Summary of amendments** Two amendments were proposed. The [first](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/download/legislation/amend/r4945_amend_8ff5e077-f708-4fc1-8b1b-df544a3658ac/upload_pdf/7410_Australian%20Education%20Bill%202013_AG.pdf;fileType=application%2Fpdf#search=%22legislation/amend/r4945_amend_8ff5e077-f708-4fc1-8b1b-df544a3658ac%22) proposes that schools apply with anti-discrimination laws. The [second](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/download/legislation/amend/r4945_amend_62e58efd-d663-4e43-9939-57f9a5c565f0/upload_pdf/7409_Australian%20Education%20Bill%202013_AG.pdf;fileType=application%2Fpdf#search=%22legislation/amend/r4945_amend_62e58efd-d663-4e43-9939-57f9a5c565f0%22) includes such proposals as schools reporting about their financial assistance. **Background to Bill** This Bill was developed in response to the [Review of Funding for Schooling](http://foi.deewr.gov.au/system/files/doc/other/review-of-funding-for-schooling-final-report-dec-2011.pdf), commissioned by [David Gonski](http://www.abc.net.au/news/2012-08-27/whats-in-the-gonski-report/4219508) (known as the 'Gonski Review'). The Report explored the issue of the decline of performance in Australian school children over the past 10 years and the gap between the highest and lowest performing students. The Report found that the current funding model for Australian schools was unnecessarily complex and proposed a new funding system. As an alternative, a new funding model was proposed. Moved the second reading of the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, describing it as part of the government's response to the first comprehensive review of school funding in almost 40 years, setting a goal of reaching the top five countries in reading, science and mathematics by 2025, with new needs-based Commonwealth funding arrangements to commence from 1 January 2014.

Opposed the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, criticising Labor's schoolkids bonus for giving secondary students $820 against just $410 for primary students despite greater returns from early investment, warning Gonski funding would not be fully committed until 2022, and called for a voucher-based system with more emphasis on science and maths, noting more than half of Chinese graduates study hard sciences compared with 17 per cent in the US.

Argued for the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, accusing Victorian education minister Martin Dixon of falsely claiming some schools would be worse off, noted every school would receive increased funding every year including an additional $4 billion overall, and recounted a constituent whose illiterate son lost access to the Reading Recovery program due to underfunding.

Opposed the rushed handling of the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill, quoting Mater Dei Catholic Primary School principal Danny Malone's questions about the government's claim that the average non-government school in New South Wales would lose $800,000 without the new funding model, and noted 71 pages of amendments were pushed through with little time for scrutiny.

Summing up debate on the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill, denied Christopher Pyne's claim of a secret means test on non-government school parents, and warned that if funding indexation fell to three per cent from the current 3.9 per cent, schools would lose $16 billion over six years.

Presented the House of Representatives Standing Committee on Education and Employment's advisory reports, with dissenting reports, on the Early Years Quality Fund Special Account Bill 2013 and the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013.

Criticised the process behind the Australian Education (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, saying the committee had only one week to assess 71 pages of amendments with no consultation, recalled Labor's 2004 hit list school funding policy under Mark Latham, and argued the Early Years Quality Fund Special Account Bill would benefit at most 40 per cent of childcare workers for only two years.

The senator argued that the government rushed the Australian Education Bill 2013 through the Senate with only 165 minutes of debate for a $16.2 billion reform, and that the new funding model would leave 469 government schools in Queensland, Victoria, and the Northern Territory worse off. He moved an amendment calling for certainty that no school would lose funding and for greater transparency, while criticising increased federal interference and red tape.
